title: Cambridge Speaking: Four Parts With a Partner
summary: Cambridge Speaking's paired, four-part format — interview, long turn, collaborative task and discussion — and the interaction skills that score.

chunks.heading: A paired test, four parts
chunks.body: Cambridge Speaking is usually taken **with another candidate and two examiners** and has **four parts**: an **interview** (personal questions), a **long individual turn** (speak alone about pictures), a **collaborative task** (discuss and decide with your partner), and a **discussion** (broader questions with the examiner).
chunks.realExample: You warm up with questions about yourself, then compare photos alone, then work with your partner toward a decision, then discuss the wider topic — a natural progression from solo to interactive.
chunks.memoryHook: Interview → long turn → collaborate with partner → discussion. You + partner + 2 examiners.

chunks.heading: The long turn — organise and fill the time
chunks.body: In the **long turn** you speak **alone for about a minute** about pictures, following the task (e.g. compare them and answer a question). **Organise your answer** and **keep talking** for the full time — a short answer leaves marks on the table.
chunks.realExample: Compare two photos: 'Both show people working, but the first is outdoors while the second… I think the first would be harder because…' — structure it and fill the minute.
chunks.memoryHook: Long turn: ~1 min alone. Organise, compare, and fill the whole time.

chunks.heading: The collaborative task — really interact
chunks.body: The **collaborative task** is where **interaction is assessed**: discuss options with your partner, **give and ask for opinions, agree and disagree politely, and work toward a decision**. Don't dominate or go silent — **turn-taking** is the skill.
chunks.realExample: 'What do you think about this option?' … 'Good point, though I'd argue…' — inviting your partner and building on their ideas scores better than delivering your own monologue.
chunks.memoryHook: Collaborate for real: invite opinions, agree/disagree, decide together. Turn-taking scores.

chunks.heading: Assessed on interactive communication
chunks.body: Examiners mark **grammar and vocabulary, discourse management, pronunciation, and interactive communication**. So beyond correct English, you're rewarded for **listening and responding, developing ideas, and keeping the conversation going** — a memorised speech won't do it.
chunks.realExample: If your partner is quiet, drawing them in ('What's your view?') actually helps your own interactive-communication mark — engagement is part of the score.
chunks.memoryHook: Marked on English AND interaction. Listen, respond, develop, keep it going.

recall.q: How is the Cambridge Speaking test set up?
recall.a: Usually with another candidate and two examiners (one asks questions, one assesses), across four parts.

recall.q: What are the four parts of Cambridge Speaking?
recall.a: An interview, a long individual turn (speaking about pictures), a collaborative task with your partner, and a discussion with the examiner.

recall.q: What should you do in the long turn?
recall.a: Speak alone for about a minute, organise your answer following the task, and keep talking to fill the whole time.

recall.q: What skill does the collaborative task assess most?
recall.a: Interaction — giving and asking for opinions, agreeing/disagreeing politely, and working toward a decision through turn-taking.

recall.q: What four things do examiners mark?
recall.a: Grammar and vocabulary, discourse management, pronunciation, and interactive communication.
